This problem is several fold.

First, understand the current new industry. They earn money though eyes on ads. The more eyes they have, the more money they make. This is a pretty simple and obvious point.

Second, is the 24hr news cycle. This was developed in because of the first point. The problem here is that there just isn't enough stuff usually happening to support the 24/7 news industry.

Third, in order to maintain the business model, they have to fill the time. This cannot happen if they just report the facts. Who, what, when, where and how now also includes analysis of what they are reporting. This introduces opinion as a 6th criteria for a story. Before, analysis was handled as an editorial or opinion piece and was sold as such.

Fourth, with the introduction of adding opinion and analysis as an element of reporting, it became apparent that not all of the viewers held the same view points as the analysts did. This had the potential to drop viewership. So you began to see the rise of opposed analysts debating news, which added manufactured drama to the story and the rise of a pundit style industry. People that make a living offering opinions and analysis.

Fifth, this led to corporations forming that would deliver news targeted towards viewers beliefs. Right wing news, left wing news, etc.

Sixth, It became apparent that news corporations would have more viewership if certain policies existed. Leftist news would earn more viewers when the left was happy, Conservative news would have more viewers when the right was happy. People don't like discouraging news, so it things were shitty for the left, viewership would drop. This led to these corporations pushing and tweaking facts to fit a mold that would appeal to their viewership. We are currently in a state where the media isn't even trying to hide it anymore. Polls are twisted to fit a narrative, stories are buried, and airtime would be skewed.

To sum it up, this was a gradual transition all tied to the first point and what that point means...more money. That's the entire motivation. True, unbiased journalism will not generate the cash that focused reporting will. Local news is the closest thing we have to journalism of old. They won't touch a lot of what we are used to from the likes of Fox News or CNN because they cannot compete and because they only have 30mins to report the day's news. In most cases, this is enough.
